newsitem.title: GERMANY: Western world coffee demand depressed in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Western world coffee demand depressed in 1996.

text.p: Coffee sales were depressed in most parts of the industrialised world, including the U.S., Europe and Japan, said James Amoroso, a Zurich-based Credit Suisse equity researcher specialising in Nestle.

"Markets are flat even after price decreases have come through and there has been a lot of promotion activity going on as well," he said. "It makes you wonder whether consumers have been lost along the way."
Amoroso was talking to Reuters during the F.O. Licht world coffee conference.
In the U.S., roast and ground sales volumes were only up one percent year-on-year in the first half of 1996 and was slowing down, he said, citing industry sources.
The soluble market, Nestle's area of business, was down four percent in Jan-June and the situation seemed to be getting worse.
In Britain, sales volumes in the soluble market were up les than one percent in the first half of 1996 but demand decreased after January in spite of price cuts.
In Germany, roast and ground market growth was flat while soluble markets grew by one percent, with the small segment of flavoured instant specialties rising five percent.
In France, soluble coffee sales were down just over half a percent in first-half 1996, but flavoured specialties sales grew by over 20 percent.
Russian sales were strong as the country's tea drinkers experimented with soluble coffees, where the preparation is similar.
Amoroso said producers would benefit from the increasing acceptance of instant coffee in China, India and the tea-drinking nations of eastern Europe.
CS equity research in a paper published on Monday reduced full year profit prospects for Nestle on the basis of disappointing first half operating performance.
It cut its earlier projections of Nestle coffee sales volume growth by three percent in 1996 to zero and to 2.5 percent in 1997 from earlier forecasts of three percent.
